                    ### Question
                    A 21-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 2-week history of progressive shortness of breath and intermittent cough with blood-tinged sputum. During this time, he has also noticed blood in his urine. He has no history of serious illness and does not take any medications. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 92/min, respirations are 28/min, and blood pressure is 152/90 mm Hg. Cardiopulmonary examination shows crackles at both lung bases. Urinalysis is positive for blood and results of a direct enzyme-linked immunoassay are positive for anti-GBM antibodies. The pathogenesis of this patient's disease is most similar to which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Henoch-Schönlein purpura
opb. Polyarteritis nodosa
opc. Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
opd. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
ope. Graft versus host disease

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's positive anti-GBM antibodies indicate Goodpasture syndrome, characterized by pulmonary hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis. This autoimmune condition involves antibody-mediated damage to the glomerular basement membrane, which is distinct from Henoch-Schönlein purpura, a small-vessel vasculitis that typically presents with skin manifestations and abdominal pain rather than pulmonary symptoms. The presence of hemoptysis and renal involvement aligns more closely with Goodpasture syndrome than with poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, which is usually preceded by a streptococcal infection and does not typically involve pulmonary hemorrhage. While polyarteritis nodosa and autoimmune hemolytic anemia involve systemic autoimmune processes, they do not specifically match the combination of lung and kidney symptoms seen in this case. Graft versus host disease is also less likely due to the absence of a transplant history. Therefore, the most similar pathogenesis to this patient's condition is Goodpasture syndrome, which is not directly represented in the options but is most closely related to the autoimmune processes described in the context of anti-GBM disease.
